title: Continuous Runtime Profiling Strategy and Playbook
author: Samir Gupta
body:
Summary
This document defines Redwood's strategy for continuous runtime profiling across the serving stack and provides an operational playbook for profiling-driven triage, kernel scheduler debugging, and benchmark validation. It is intended for runtime engineers, SREs, and ML infra engineers who maintain model serving performance.

Goals
- Establish a low-overhead, continuous sampling and tracing pipeline that captures production signals relevant to latency, memory, and kernel scheduling.
- Provide deterministic procedures for reproducing and isolating hot-path performance regressions.
- Define ownership, retention, and alerting rules so profiling becomes a first-class SLO diagnostic.

Scope
This covers: serving runtime components (request router, shard manager, KV cache, kernel executor), GPU/CPU kernel telemetry, continuous sampling agents, profiling data storage, and on-call playbooks. It does NOT cover client-side SDK profiling or offline model training workloads.

Signals & Instrumentation
1) Metrics to collect (examples):
  - Per-request p50/p95/p99 latency (generate, stream finish)
  - Per-shard GPU utilization and memory fraction
  - Kernel queue lag (ms) and kernel execution time histograms
  - KV cache hit/miss latencies and hit ratios
  - Batch size distribution (tokens/req) and batch wait time
2) Traces & events:
  - Request span with tags: request_id, model_id, shard_id, kernel_variant, seq_len, routing_policy
  - Kernel-level events annotated with NVTX/CUPTI IDs for GPU kernels and eBPF markers for CPU paths
3) Sampling strategies:
  - Low-overhead continuous sampling: 1% of requests (configurable per-customer tier) for full traces; aggregated metrics for all requests.
  - Adaptive burst sampling: increase sampling to 10–25% for requests hitting a latency anomaly window (automated).
  - Per-kernel micro-sampling: capture 100ms windows of raw kernel timing every 5 minutes per GPU to profile jitter.

Profiling Data Pipeline
- Collectors: lightweight sidecar (go agent) + eBPF probes on host + CUPTI/NVTX for GPU kernels.
- Transport: buffered protobuf over gRPC to central ingestion cluster with back-pressure and local disk buffering for network partitions.
- Storage: short-term hot storage (7 days) for full traces; aggregated histograms and flamegraph artifacts retained for 90 days; long-term cold archive (1 year) for selected traces.
- Analysis: automated job that computes heatmaps (kernel hotness, shard hotshifts) nightly and writes artifacts to S3 and dashboard bundles.

Operational Playbook: High-level Triage (on-call)
1) Alert receives: increased p99 for generate endpoint (> latency SLO by 2x for 5 minutes).
2) Quick triage (first 6 minutes):
  - Check dashboard: cluster-level GPU utilization, queue depth, and recent kernel error rates.
  - Inspect request-distribution: any single model_id or shard_id contributing > 60% of p99?
  - Check recent rollout or config changes via /release-notes.
3) If no config change: escalate to profiling-run (step 4).
4) Profiling-run (10–30 minutes):
  - Trigger an adaptive sampling increase for affected shard(s): POST /internal/observe/sampling {"shard_id":"s-123", "rate":0.2, "duration":900}
  - Collect 20 full traces and per-kernel NVTX timelines.
  - Run isolated microbench on a staging shard with identical model variant (see Reproduce section).
5) Mitigations:
  - If kernel queue lag identified: apply fast fallback policy to alternative kernel variant (config path: /services/kernel-scheduler/fallbacks).
  - If memory spike on KV cache: increase eviction aggressiveness and pin small-hotset caches.
  - If GPU memory fragmentation: restart affected worker(s) during low-traffic window using graceful-drain.

Reproduce Locally / Running Microbenchmarks
- Use the bench harness in eng-serving-runtime/benchmarking-and-perf-suite: repo command:
  ./bench run --model <model> --seq-len 2048 --batch-sizes "[1,4,8]" --trace-nvtx --out artifacts/<run-id>
- Example:
  ./bench run --model redwood-7b-v1 --seq-len 1024 --batch-sizes "[1,2,4]" --trace-nvtx --out artifacts/run-20260203
- Collect kernel timings with nvprof-style wrapper:
  NVPROF_OUTPUT=artifacts/run-20260203/nvprof ./bench run ...
- For CPU kernel traces use: sudo bpftool prog loadall scripts/ebpf/probes.o /sys/fs/bpf/probes
  && ./bench run --cpu-profiling

Kernel Scheduling Debug Recipe
- Symptoms: sudden p99 increases but GPU utilization is stable; queue depth grows with small batches.
- Steps:
  1) Identify candidate kernels from aggregated heatmap (last 1h).
  2) Correlate kernel_variant with scheduling decisions in scheduler log (/var/log/kernel-scheduler.log). Use grep for request_id.
  3) Temporarily enable detailed scheduler audit for one node: /internal/kernel-scheduler/audit?node=n-12&level=debug (5 minutes).
  4) If preemption thrashing observed, increase kernel-runtime spin threshold from 8ms -> 20ms for the problematic variant. Rollback after test.

Benchmarks and Acceptance Criteria
- Nightly microbench run matrix: top 10 models across representative seq_lens and batch sizes. Expected baselines stored in benchmarks/canonical/<date>.json.
- Release gating: no model-serving release may be promoted if any nightly benchmark shows >10% regression in median latency or >5% increase in 99th latency for two consecutive runs.
- Canary rollout: enable 1% traffic to new scheduler with increased logging for 24h; monitor kernel hotness and p99 delta.

Known Pitfalls & Gotchas
- NVTX-only traces miss kernel queueing that happens at the CUDA driver boundary; enable CUPTI sampling when investigating queue buildup.
- eBPF probes can add CPU overhead if attached to high-frequency syscalls; restrict to targeted nodes.
- Running microbenchmarks on shared GPUs will produce noisy results; always use isolated nodes or dedicated reserved capacity.

Dashboards & Alerts (examples)
- Dashboards: "Runtime Heatmap" (kernel vs shard), "GPU Queue Depth" (per-pod histogram), "Batching Health" (tokens/sec, batch wait).
- Alerts: p99 generate > SLO*1.5 for 5m (pager), GPU kernel errors > 0.5% over 10m (page+slack), persistent kernel scheduler preemption rate > baseline+2 sigma (ticket).

Release Checklist (profiling-specific)
- New kernel variant reviewed and annotated with NVTX tags.
- Microbench results validated against canonical baselines.
- Canary config included in rollout plan and profiling sampling enabled for canary nodes.
- Team owner assigned to monitor first-24h: owner oncall:eng-serving-runtime.

Ownership & Contact
- Document owner: Samir Gupta (runtime infra).
- Primary teams: eng-serving-runtime (primary), eng-sre (alerts/instrumentation), applied-ml-and-evals (benchmark validation).
- Slack channels: #runtime-profiling, #gpu-ops.

Appendix: Useful commands and snippets
- Increase sampling locally (dev):
  curl -X POST -H 'Authorization: Bearer $DEV_TOKEN' "https://internal-api.redwood/company/observe/sampling" -d '{"service":"runtime","rate":0.1}'
- Example NVTX span in C++ kernel wrapper:
  NVTX_RANGE_PUSHA("kernel_attn_v1_forward");
  run_kernel(...);
  NVTX_RANGE_POP();
- Flamegraph generation (after collecting stacks):
  stackcollapse.pl perf.stacks > perf.folded
  flamegraph.pl perf.folded > perf.svg

- Profiling guidelines: profiling-playbook/runtime-profiling-playbook-guidelines-2025
